title: 2010-26 — Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained; the SJC held KEP's dismissal of TE Lee's charges without trial was not constitutionally permissible and remanded for action consistent with its decision, requiring KEP to begin process under BCO 32 unless it could document a constitutional basis for dismissal. The SJC rejected KEP's judicial out-of-order defense and denied Lee's request that the SJC enter guilt verdicts, holding that power exists only in an appeal, not a complaint.
first_summary: Korean Eastern Presbytery dismissed TE Eliot Lee's charges against two teaching elders without trial; the SJC sustained Lee's complaint and remanded. The SJC reasoned KEP failed to show a constitutional basis for dismissing properly filed charges. It declined Lee's request to enter guilt findings.
summary: Korean Eastern Presbytery dismissed TE Eliot Lee's charges against two teaching elders without trial, and the SJC sustained Lee's complaint that this was unconstitutional. Although a presbytery may dismiss charges under BCO 29-1, 32-20, 34-2, or 31-8, it bears the burden of documenting that basis; KEP did not. The SJC refused Lee's request that it enter the guilt verdicts the presbytery should have reached—that power exists on appeal, not complaint. It remanded for KEP to begin process under BCO 32.

sources.supports: Case identity, facts, issue, judgment sustaining the complaint and remanding, SJC reasoning, vote, and qualifications.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2010-26, Lee v. Korean Eastern Presbytery, decided by the SJC, 40th GA (2012); the decision was written jointly and adopted as amended by the full SJC, with 19 concurring, 2 dissenting, 1 not qualified, 1 disqualified, and 1 absent (lines 1, 194–200; printed p. 538).
evidence_notes.dispute: TE Lee filed charges in January 2009 against two KEP teaching elders; KEP dismissed the charges on 6/2/09 and later dismissed Lee's complaint on 10/5/10 without trial, prompting Lee's complaint to the General Assembly (lines 17–23, 43–55; printed pp. 530–533).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC answered yes and remanded; it held that a presbytery may dismiss properly filed charges only under BCO 29-1, 32-20, 34-2, or 31-8, with the burden on the presbytery to document its reasoning in the record, and that KEP did not meet that burden. KEP was required to begin process under BCO 32-2 and 32-3 unless it made the required showing (lines 57–59, 83–116, 143–190; printed pp. 533–538).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC rejected KEP's judicial out-of-order argument because this matter continued prior complaint 2009-16 and KEP had acted on it (lines 63–67; printed pp. 533–534). It denied Lee's request to render guilt verdicts, noting that power exists only in an appeal, not a complaint, and that the record lacked evidence beyond Lee's charges (lines 69–81; printed p. 534). It also noted possible but unproven BCO 31-8 concerns about Lee (lines 118–141; printed pp. 535–536).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The decision references prior SJC cases 2007-9, 2007-10, 2007-11, and 2009-16 as established background and authority, but no operative incorporated judgment is supplied in this source (lines 15, 23, 29–41, 63–67, 80–81, 101–102, 112, 123).
